item.title: Shopkeepers raise alarm over unpaid teachers forced to buy on credit, FTA members could call for industrial action
item.description: Shopkeepers have been calling the Fijian Teachers Association to raise concerns about teachers who are being forced to buy goods on credit because they have not received their salaries, and FTA's members could call for industrial action if the issue remains unresolved. This has been shared to fijivillage News by the General Secretary of the Fiji Teachers Association, Paula Manumanunitoga.
item.content:encoded:
Shopkeepers have been calling the Fijian Teachers Association to raise concerns about teachers who are being forced to buy goods on credit because they have not received their salaries, and FTA's members could call for industrial action if the issue remains unresolved.

This has been shared to fijivillage News by the General Secretary of the Fiji Teachers Association, Paula Manumanunitoga.

He says the failure to pay workers on time is a serious concern under the Employment Relations Act.

Manumanunitoga says the situation is extremely serious, with some teachers going for several months without getting paid by the Ministry of Education after taking up appointments, particularly those posted to the outer islands.

According to Manumanunitoga, newly appointed teachers receive their appointment letters and travel to their assigned schools, often having to make arrangements to reach remote communities by boat however, some reportedly wait one, two, three, or even four months before receiving their first salary.

He says in some cases, teachers have accumulated nearly $1,000 in credit.

Manumanunitoga says once a person has been appointed and begins working, they are expected to receive their salaries.

He says the association has questioned why the current backlog has occurred, noting that in the past, appointment letters were sent directly to the relevant salaries section so that payments can be processed.

The General Secretary says following discussions with the Permanent Secretary, the association was given an undertaking that teachers who have not received their salaries would be paid in Pay 17.

The association is calling for those responsible for the delays to be identified and held accountable, saying the situation cannot be allowed to continue.

There is also growing concern about what could happen if teachers are not paid as promised.

The FTA is urging the Ministry of Education and Ministry of Finance to ensure that all outstanding salaries, including acting allowances, are paid as promised.

Minister for Education, Aseri Radrodro highlighted earlier this week that salary arrears owed to 318 Ministry of Education staff will be expedited and processed through Pay 17 and Pay 18.

Radrodro assured all affected teachers and Ministry of Education staff that the necessary processes are underway to facilitate the payment of these outstanding salary arrears.

He acknowledged the concerns and difficulties experienced by staff as a result of the delays.

The Minister says these delays have been due to internal processing and compliance requirements necessary to ensure that all payments are properly verified and processed accurately and efficiently.

He says to support the timely processing of payments, all affected teachers are encouraged to ensure that their documentation is complete and up to date, including proper appointment documentation, FTRA registration certificates, correct bank account details and confirmation of commencement dates from Heads of Schools and/or District Education Officers.

He says the Ministry has undertaken the necessary due diligence to ensure that appointments are properly formalised and that all required documentation is in place before payments are processed.

Radrodro says welfare of their staff remains a priority for the Ministry.

item.title: Start conserving water now as drier conditions expected – Fiji Met
item.description: Fijians are being urged to start conserving water, as below-normal rainfall is expected over the next three to six months which could put pressure on water supplies. Fiji Meteorological Service Scientific Climate Officer Shweta Shiwangni says El Niño typically brings drier conditions to Fiji, with the Western Division usually feeling the effects first before they spread to other parts of the count
item.content:encoded:
Fijians are being urged to start conserving water, as below-normal rainfall is expected over the next three to six months which could put pressure on water supplies.

Fiji Meteorological Service Scientific Climate Officer Shweta Shiwangni says El Niño typically brings drier conditions to Fiji, with the Western Division usually feeling the effects first before they spread to other parts of the country.

Shiwangni says people should start practising water conservation and carefully manage how they use available water resources.

She says while Fiji will still receive some rainfall during this period, it may not be enough to meet the country's usual needs.

Shiwangni says the drier conditions could also affect farmers, particularly those who rely on water for irrigation.

She says Energy Fiji Limited will also need to manage water levels in its hydroelectric catchments as the dry conditions continue.

The current outlook indicates El Niño conditions will remain active in Fiji's part of the world for the rest of 2026 and into early 2027.

The Fiji Meteorological Service releases monthly climate bulletins to government agencies, non-government organisations and other stakeholders.

Shiwangni says agencies can request meetings with the Fiji Meteorological Service based on the outlook, where they are provided with updates on El Niño conditions and expected rainfall.

Her comments come as stakeholders meet at the Weather Ready Nation Fiji Workshop in Suva to improve preparedness and how weather and climate information is used to help communities respond to potential impacts.

Hibiscus Festival Director, Ellen Whippy-Knight says the purpose of this evening was a media launch of the partnership between the contestants and their sponsors.
item.content:encoded:
It was a night of glitz and glamour as the 70th Anniversary of the FMF Hibiscus Festival was launched this evening at the Civic Centre where the Queen contestants took centre stage with their sponsors.

Hibiscus Festival Director, Ellen Whippy-Knight says the purpose of this evening was a media launch of the partnership between the contestants and their sponsors.

Whippy-Knight says it is a concept they created last year where the sponsor actually comes up and presents their contestant and vice versa.

She says it was also a very entertaining and a wonderful opportunity to see how the contestants have progressed from the weeks of training prior to this.

The Festival Director says taking the Hibiscus Festival back to Albert Park has been something that everybody in Suva has been looking forward to.

Insert: Whippy-Knight on contestants Aug 13

The Hibiscus Festival will start on 29th August at Albert Park in Suva.

item.title: 65-year-old Suva man gets second chance at life after heart surgery
item.description: It was good news and a moment of relief for 65-year-old Bhupendra Kumar and his family of Suva, after he recently underwent coronary artery bypass grafting surgery at Pacific Specialist Healthcare in Nadi. Kumar says he underwent the surgery last Friday, which gave him a second chance at life.
item.content:encoded:
It was good news and a moment of relief for 65-year-old Bhupendra Kumar and his family of Suva, after he recently underwent coronary artery bypass grafting surgery at Pacific Specialist Healthcare in Nadi.

Kumar says he underwent the surgery last Friday, which gave him a second chance at life.

He says after returning to Fiji from an overseas trip, he started experiencing sharp chest pain and required complex four-vessel coronary artery bypass surgery following medical tests.

He says his family initially considered getting him treated overseas.

However, this would have put extra pressure on him and could have caused his condition to deteriorate due to the long-distance travel.

Kumar says the turning point came when a family friend recommended them Pacific Specialist Healthcare in Nadi.

He adds that after a thorough consultation with the chief surgeon, the family made the decision to have the surgery done in Fiji.

Kumar says he had never thought that something like this could be done locally as well.

While acknowledging the nurses and the surgeon for their support, Kumar says he is now recovering well.

Pacific Specialist Healthcare Cardiothoracic and Vascular Surgeon Dr Sanjeev Kumar Khubley says they have conducted seven heart surgeries this month, including five coronary artery bypass graft procedures, commonly known as CABG, one mediastinal tumour excision and one mitral valve replacement.

He says they are preparing to carry out more procedures in the coming week.

item.title: Fiji cannot build its tourism future if it keeps losing skilled workers overseas - Gavoka
item.description: Fiji cannot build a sustainable tourism industry if it continues to train skilled hospitality workers only to lose them overseas, with the Government acknowledging that better pay and opportunities are driving young Fijians abroad and saying more must be done to create rewarding careers that make staying in Fiji a worthwhile choice. Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Tourism and Civil Aviation
item.content:encoded:
Fiji cannot build a sustainable tourism industry if it continues to train skilled hospitality workers only to lose them overseas, with the Government acknowledging that better pay and opportunities are driving young Fijians abroad and saying more must be done to create rewarding careers that make staying in Fiji a worthwhile choice.

Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Tourism and Civil Aviation Viliame Gavoka highlighted this while addressing 153 students graduating from the ServicePro International Tourism and Hospitality Institute with Certificate III qualifications in Kitchen Operations and Hospitality Operations.

Gavoka says Fiji is seeing some of its finest young people, including trained cooks, skilled housekeepers, waiters and hospitality workers, leave the country for opportunities abroad.

He says this brain drain hurts Fiji, particularly when the country invests in training people who later take their skills overseas.

However, Gavoka says he understands why young Fijians choose to leave, as salaries can be higher and there are opportunities to gain international experience.

He says he would never blame a young Fijian for wanting more for their family.

Gavoka says those who decide to work overseas should learn as much as they can and eventually bring that knowledge and experience back to Fiji.

He says Fiji also needs to face the reality that it cannot build its future around continually training people and then losing them.

The Tourism Minister says around 75,000 visitors arrive in Fiji every month, highlighting the continuing demand for skilled workers across the tourism industry.

He says these numbers should not simply be viewed as statistics but as opportunities for young Fijians to build long-term careers in tourism and hospitality.

Gavoka says the Government wants to create an industry where staying in Fiji does not mean sacrificing career development or a better standard of living.

He says Fiji's sustainable tourism plans are focused on building a prosperous visitor economy, thriving and inclusive communities, protecting what makes Fiji unique and ensuring the country's islands and oceans remain healthy.

Gavoka says these objectives are also about ensuring Fijians working in tourism do not simply have jobs, but have opportunities to share in the wealth created by the industry and progress through their careers.

He says the aim is to create pathways where a young person entering the industry as a cook today can become a head chef tomorrow and potentially own their own business in the future.

The Minister says Fiji does not want its people to become the cheapest pair of hands in someone else's resort, but skilled and respected professionals who can build successful careers of their own.

Gavoka says investment is also being made to spread tourism opportunities beyond Fiji's traditional tourism areas.

He highlighted tourism development in Vanua Levu as an important part of creating opportunities in the North so young people can pursue careers closer to their communities instead of having to leave their island.

Gavoka also highlighted the importance of Tourism Fiji's international marketing efforts in keeping Fiji visible in global markets, attracting visitors and supporting continued industry growth.

He says tourism growth should also benefit other sectors of the economy, including farmers and fishers.

Through initiatives linking farms and local producers directly with hotels and restaurants, Gavoka says more of what visitors eat can be produced locally.

He says resorts are increasingly growing produce such as herbs, chillies, pawpaw and dalo and turning locally grown food into memorable experiences for visitors.

Gavoka says when this happens, the benefits of tourism remain within Fiji, as the land feeds the kitchen, the kitchen feeds the visitor and visitor spending ultimately supports local communities.

He has urged the 153 graduates to remain proud of their profession, continue learning, maintain high standards and protect Fiji's unique spirit of hospitality.

Gavoka says whether graduates choose to remain in Fiji or gain experience overseas before returning, the country needs their skills.

He says every young Fijian who chooses to stay, develop their skills and progress through the industry represents a victory for Fiji and, over time, those individual successes can help change the country's future.

item.title: Charters' 7 devices re-seized by Police, High Court motion filed after the seizure
item.description: Fijian and British national, Charlie Charters has filed a High Court motion after the Fiji Police Force returned seven seized electronic devices to Charters’ lawyer on Friday after the investigation against him was ended in the High Court, only for Fiji Police to immediately re-seize them under a fresh court order. The seven devices include medical apps for the treatment and management of Charters
item.content:encoded:
Fijian and British national, Charlie Charters has filed a High Court motion after the Fiji Police Force returned seven seized electronic devices to Charters’ lawyer on Friday after the investigation against him was ended in the High Court, only for Fiji Police to immediately re-seize them under a fresh court order.

The seven devices include medical apps for the treatment and management of Charters’ throat cancer and heart condition that he has not been able to access for six months, as well as financial and payment Apps and hard drives on which his work product is stored.

Charters says you have always got to be braced for Fiji’s capacity to surprise but even they were shocked by what happened to his lawyer, Seforan Fatiaki when he presented himself to CID on Friday.

He says the investigation by FICAC has been thoroughly discredited in the High Court so it seems truly bizarre where this is going now.

Fatiaki had first applied to FICAC in writing for the return of the devices on March 16th.

In court on Friday August 7th, Magistrate Shageeth Somaratne ordered the Fiji Police to return the devices to Charters’ lawyer.

The devices had been seized a day after FICAC’s February 21st detention and arrest at Nadi Airport, and their subsequent charging of Charters, which was permanently stayed by the High Court on July 24th.

Charters says the Police do not appear to have understood Justice Pita Bulamainaivalu’s ruling.

He says the charges against him were stayed by the High Court for a number of reasons including that, in the absence of any law limiting his rights, we all enjoy the right of freedom of speech, expression, thought, opinion and publication under section 17 of the Constitution.

Charters says the judge has said that when expressing those rights, we also have the right not to divulge the sources of our journalistic information.

He also alleges there were significant errors in the search warrant documentation which would be part of the submissions that would be argued in the High Court action.

item.title: Police lead, RFMF provides support in joint operations - Tikoduadua
item.description: The Republic of Fiji Military Forces remains in a supporting role as it conducts joint operations with the Fiji Police Force, with police continuing to take the lead on the ground. Minister for Defence Pio Tikoduadua says the arrangement is not new, with the RFMF stepping in when additional manpower and specialised capabilities are required.
item.content:encoded:
The Republic of Fiji Military Forces remains in a supporting role as it conducts joint operations with the Fiji Police Force, with police continuing to take the lead on the ground.

Minister for Defence Pio Tikoduadua says the arrangement is not new, with the RFMF stepping in when additional manpower and specialised capabilities are required.

INSERT: Minister on RFMF provides support PN 13th Aug

Tikoduadua says while joint operations involving the RFMF can be expensive, the military has capabilities that can provide critical support when needed.

He highlighted the use of drones by the Republic of Fiji Navy , particularly during search and rescue operations where visibility and weather conditions allow them to be deployed.
